title: Add demo tenant Terraform module + example (quotas, routes/fallback, dashboards)
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Internal: Adds a reusable Terraform module + working example to provision the Standard Demo v1 tenant resources (quotas, routes w/ fallback, and imported dashboards) in a repeatable, idempotent way.
description: Summary: This PR adds a first-pass Terraform module and a runnable example to provision the Standard Demo v1 “demo tenant” resources in a repeatable way. The goal is to reduce SE heroics and make demo tenant setup/reset idempotent (ENG-4920), with a consistent set of guardrails (quotas/rate limits), scenario routing + fallback, and “known good” dashboards (ENG-4922). Motivation: We’ve had drift across regions and manual Console edits causing missing panels / broken queries (INT-782) and inconsistent routing behavior during dry runs. This module establishes a single source of truth for what the demo tenant should look like and makes it easy to recreate in a fresh environment without clicking through the Console. What’s included: (1) modules/demo_tenant: creates/updates a tenant-level quota policy, per-route overrides, and a small set of named routes used by the talk track (hosted baseline route + a canary route + a fallback route). (2) Routing/fallback: a “primary” route pinned to a known-good model version + quant profile, with a compatible fallback (same family, slightly lower cost) and a region fallback policy (primary region -> secondary region) for capacity issues. (3) Dashboard import: ships exported dashboard JSON in dashboards/demo_tenant/*.json and creates dashboard resources with stable UIDs/titles to avoid duplicates across applies. (4) examples/demo-tenant-standard-v1: end-to-end example wiring with minimal variables; includes a README that matches the expected pre-demo checklist (apply, verify dashboards, export outputs for the driver). (5) Safety: avoids outputting secrets by default; API keys are passed in via provider auth and the example only outputs tenant_id, route IDs, and dashboard URLs. How it works: The module composes existing provider resources (tenant, quota_policy, route, route_fallback_policy, dashboard) and uses local files for dashboard JSON. Route naming is stable and includes a prefix var so we can run “demo-na”, “demo-emea”, etc without collisions. Testing: terraform fmt/validate, tflint, and a basic plan/apply smoke test in CI against the sandbox control-plane endpoint (no real GPU capacity required). Also verified a clean destroy/apply does not create duplicate dashboards and does not re-order route rules. Rollout plan: After merge, Rafael will run this in the demo tenant sandbox workspace and we’ll swap the runbook to point to the module usage. Follow-ups: (a) add a small ‘reset’ wrapper script that re-applies + re-seeds scenario data (tracked in ENG-4920), (b) wire weekly regression to run terraform plan and alert on drift (ENG-4923), (c) extend the module with optional EU-only routing constraints for EMEA asks.
commits: terraform: add demo_tenant module skeleton + variables
routing: add primary+fallback routes with stable naming
quotas: add default demo quota policy + per-route overrides
dashboards: add imported JSON dashboards + README verification steps
ci: add tflint + validate workflow for module/example
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): “Can we ensure dashboards don’t duplicate on each apply? We got burned by this last week.” Priya Natarajan (author): “Yep — added stable uid per dashboard and made title deterministic. Also added a note in README to verify you don’t see duplicates after a second apply.” Logan Wright (Telemetry): “The errors panel in errors-and-throttles.json is missing 429 breakdown, which is a common demo failure mode.” Priya: “Good catch. Added 429 series split by route_id and updated panel description to match the talk track.” Cole Summers (Quotas): “Default quotas look high; we want demo-safe defaults to avoid runaway spend if someone runs a loop.” Priya: “Lowered default token/min caps and added per-route overrides for the streaming scenario route. Also added an explicit ‘burst’ flag variable default=false that prevents high caps unless intentionally set.” Mina Haddad (Routing): “Fallback policy should distinguish between model unavailability and quota throttles; we should not automatically fail over on 429.” Priya: “Agreed. Updated policy conditions: failover triggers only on 5xx + capacity_unavailable + timeout; not on 429. README now includes ‘if you see 429, stop and reset quotas’.” Markus Klein (SE): “Example output should include direct Console URLs for routes/dashboards so the driver can click fast.” Priya: “Added outputs for route_console_url and dashboard_console_url (non-sensitive), and included copy/paste snippet in README.” Rafael Mendes (Runbook owner): “Please add a callout on required IAM/RBAC role for applying this.” Priya: “Added ‘demo_tenant_admin’ requirement and least-privilege scope in module README. Also documented that API keys should not be stored in state.” Final approvals: Sean approved after second round; Mina + Cole approved after condition tweak; Logan approved after 429 panel addition; Markus approved after outputs update. Priya squashed and merged.
post_merge_notes: Action item: update the Demo Tenant Setup Runbook to reference examples/demo-tenant-standard-v1 and remove manual Console steps for quotas/routes/dashboards. Owners: Rafael Mendes + Markus Klein.
